newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean won ends lower on high dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: South Korean won ends lower on high dollar demand.

text.p: An oversupply of the South Korean won sent the currency to close lower against the dollar on Tuesday as import settlements continued to outstrip export deals, dealers said.

The central Bank of Korea's dollar-selling intervention did not correct the situation, they added. The central bank has never acknowledged stepping into the market. The won ended at 848.50, after opening at 848.00. During the day, it touched a high of 847.80 and sank to 848.70, the lowest level seen since a market average system was instituted in March 1990.
Though many dealers have said the won was suffering from large importer settlements, a western bank trader disagreed.
"Rather than huge importer settlement, I think we're witnessing a decrease in exporter deals," he said.
The dollar's strength on the world market also added pressure on the won.
Traders said the won was seen moving in a 847.50-848.70 range on Wednesday. "I think the central bank will actively gaurd the 849.00 level," said a local bank dealer.
The base mid-rate was seen at 848.30 on Wednesday, compared to Tuesday's 847.50. -- KATHERINE BRUCE (822) 727 5644
